conflicts_resolved: Australian couples: readers proposed 'clients', 'hosts' or a trim. Brand-facts allows only the trim on a birthday page, so 'quoting in AUD' (p01); 'clients' and 'hosts' rejected as new wording.

Candle and sunscreen lines: primary persona wanted them cut to one line; the sceptic valued the linked sources. Shortened, not removed, so each fact marker keeps an accurate claim and its link (p02, p03).

Closing opener: primary's replacement compared the birthday to a destination wedding (wedding framing, which the brief avoids near Advisor lines); the sceptic's plainer lead-in chosen, shortened (p07).
'The pace is the point': sceptic called it a slogan; the primary persona singled it out as how they want a weekend to feel. Kept.
'Several months': planner wanted a range, sceptic preferred honesty over a made-up figure. Kept, as no sourced range exists.
UHNW scale and privacy asks: applied only as ideas or questions to the venue and host advice (p06, p11, p13); nothing claims Wedded Concierge scale, security or confidentiality.
payload.gate_note: Weighted enquiry likelihood 2.1 is below 3.8 and there were must_fix items, so revise. Fast mode allows one round: after these 13 edits the writer produces 08-final.md and the gap is accepted, not re-paneled. Enquiry is held down mainly by business details deliberately deferred for this post: Fees and commissions; Deposit protection and who holds client money; Who is on the ground and on-the-day phone contact; Named people and real birthday examples (proof for 'anywhere in the world'); Scale (200+ guests, several countries), security and confidentiality processes; Transfers we provide, room blocks and Wedded Privileges; Availability and whether a party at home is in scope; Whether the Advisor can work with an assistant or family office. None of these may be added.

edits.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner (Advisor body line)
edits.old: quoting in AUD for Australian couples
edits.reason: Raised by all five readers: 'couples' reads as wedding copy on a birthday page and 'Australian' excludes families split across countries. Trimmed per brand-facts 'quotes in AUD for Australian couples'; no new wording.

edits.section: An intimate dinner at home (candle safety)
edits.old: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper, and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the [SA Metropolitan Fire Service candle fact sheet](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) sets out. <!-- fact_04 --> <!-- fact_05 --> A draught can melt wax unevenly and tip a candle over, so on a terrace or near an open door, battery candles are a safe alternative. <!-- fact_05 --> <!-- fact_06 -->
edits.new: A candle is an open flame. Keep linen, florals and paper well clear of each one and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the [SA Metropolitan Fire Service candle fact sheet](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) sets out. <!-- fact_04 --> <!-- fact_05 --> On a terrace or near an open door, where a draught can make a candle melt unevenly and tip, battery candles are a safe alternative. <!-- fact_05 --> <!-- fact_06 -->
edits.reason: Four readers found the safety block longer than the idea and pamphlet in tone. Split and shortened; source link and each fact marker keep an accurate claim (open flame, keep clear, non-combustible holders, draught, battery candles).

edits.section: A long lunch or garden party (sunscreen)
edits.old: Leave SPF50+ sunscreen and hats at the entrance. Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours, or after swimming or heavy sweating. <!-- fact_03 -->
edits.new: Leave SPF50+ sunscreen and hats at the entrance so guests can reapply every two hours through the afternoon. <!-- fact_03 -->
edits.reason: Three readers (incl. primary) read the application instructions as a school note. Keeps the hosting gesture and the sourced two-hour reapplication claim, so fact_03 stays accurate.

edits.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event (venue questions)
edits.old: - What will you confirm in writing, and when?
edits.new:
- What deposit is needed, when is the balance due, and what happens to it if you cancel or the date moves?
- What will you confirm in writing, and when?
edits.reason: Money trust gap (funding parent, medium): the checklist never mentions deposits or cancellation. Added as a question to the venue only; no figures or brand claims.

edits.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event (venue questions)
edits.old: How are dietary and accessibility needs handled, and are candles allowed?
edits.new: How are dietary and accessibility needs handled, including a route without steps to every space you will use, and are candles allowed?
edits.reason: Funding parent: 'accessibility' alone is too vague to put to a venue. Question only.

edits.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event (venue questions)
edits.old: - Is it exclusive use, or are spaces shared with other guests?
edits.new: - Is it exclusive use, or are spaces shared with other guests? Can the whole property be closed to the public for your stay?
edits.reason: UHNW: the natural next question on exclusive use. Question to the venue only, no scale or security claim.

edits.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge (close opener)
edits.old: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
edits.new: If you would rather hand over the planning, this is what that looks like.
edits.reason: Planner couple (primary) and sceptic both flagged the opener as filler. Plain lead-in to the Advisor close; adds no brand facts.

edits.section: Choosing a place guests can reach (Smartraveller)
edits.old: which recommends you subscribe to the destinations you're visiting, including where you're transiting through.
edits.new: and subscribe to updates for each destination on the route, including places you transit through, as it recommends.
edits.reason: Primary persona needed two reads. Same meaning and source; fact_12 claim intact.

edits.section: FAQ, What are the milestone birthdays
edits.old: The birthdays that mark a new decade, along with any age the person sees as a turning point.
edits.new: The decade birthdays, such as the 30th, 40th, 50th and 60th, along with any age the person sees as a turning point.
edits.reason: Search visitor: the answer was vaguer than the intro. Names only the ages already in the intro.

edits.section: Celebrating a milestone as a couple
edits.old: A joint celebration halves the travel for guests and doubles the reason to come.
edits.new: A joint celebration means guests make one trip instead of two, with two reasons to come.
edits.reason: Sceptic: loose quantitative claim. Stated literally.

edits.old: A long weekend with close friends at a villa or a small hotel
edits.new: A long weekend with close friends at a villa, a small hotel or a whole property taken for the group
edits.reason: UHNW: the idea assumed small scale. Adds an option, not a claim about our scale; 'The pace is the point' kept (primary persona praised it).

edits.old: and one evening when everyone sits down together.
edits.new: and one evening when everyone sits down together. Ask the family early about customs, food requirements and timings that matter to them, so the menu and the schedule fit.
edits.reason: UHNW: shows awareness of family customs by asking rather than assuming.

edits.section: Planning a milestone birthday for someone else
edits.old: For a surprise, say clearly what must stay secret and keep it off social media.
edits.new: For a surprise, say clearly what must stay secret and keep it off social media. Even without a surprise, some families would rather nothing is shared; say so in the invitation and ask the venue and suppliers to respect it.
edits.reason: UHNW: privacy as a default, written as host advice. Makes no confidentiality claim about Wedded Concierge.
